_readme: A123 (Satkirti msg 6848/6849, 27.10.2026): English translation + word-by-word for the 7 ārati songs of book.json (61 verses), which had IAST only. Applied by en_apply.py (only «translation» and «wbw» of these verses in data/book.json; IAST, RU and other languages untouched). TRANSLATION of every verse: verbatim from «Śrī Gauḍīya Gīti-guccha», Gauḍīya Vedānta Publications, 7th ed. 2016 (English; …/Библиотека/Гаудия Веданта (Нараяна Махарадж)/Шри Гаудия-гити-гуччха (GVP, 7-е изд. 2016, англ., сокращ.).pdf) — the same songbook the Russian translations come from (rule 115: «Песенник гаудия-вайшнава», Воронеж 2015, по «Шри Гаудия-гити-гуччхе»). Corrections of evident misprints (rule 31) are listed per song in «translation_edits». WORD-BY-WORD: per song in «wbw_source» — kksongs.org «Word for word» (BBT-style synonyms) where it exists and agrees with the GGG translation; otherwise composed by Purohita Lipikāra (Mantrī A123) from the IAST and the GGG translation, with the same word division as the Russian пословный перевод of book.ru-iast.json.

song-gurvastakam.translation_source: Śrī Gauḍīya Gīti-guccha (GVP, 7th ed. 2016), «Śrī Gurvāṣṭakam», pp. 255–257
song-gurvastakam.wbw_source: kksongs.org/synonym/s/samsaradavanala.html (BBT-style synonyms); spelling only: ḿ/ń → ṁ/ṅ, «dāvā-anala» → «dāva-anala», «sada» → «sadā», «Brahma Muhurta» → «brāhma-muhūrta», «Vrndavana» → «Vṛndāvana»; v9 «etad — like this» → «this», «in great care» → «with great care»

verses.translation: To deliver the living beings scorched by the blazing forest fire of material existence, śrī gurudeva, who is an ocean of auspicious qualities, manifests like a condensed cloud of mercy. I adore the lotus feet of that śrī gurudeva.

verses.translation: His heart intoxicated in the prema-rasa of Śrīman Mahāprabhu’s kīrtana, śrī guru dances, sings, and plays various instruments. Becoming intoxicated by love, his hair stands on end, he shivers, and sheds torrents of tears. I adore the lotus feet of that śrī gurudeva.

verses.translation: Śrī gurudeva always worships and serves śrī vigraha, dressing and decorating Them in varieties of raiments and ornaments (that stimulate Their śṛṅgāra-rasa) and performing other services such as cleansing the temple. He also engages the devotees (under his guidance) in these services. I adore the lotus feet of that śrī gurudeva.
verses.wbw: śrī-vigraha — (of) the arcā-vigraha (Deities); ārādhana — the worship; nitya — daily; nānā — (with) various; śṛṅgāra — clothing and ornaments; tat — of the Lord; mandira — (of) the temple; mārjana-ādau — in the cleaning, etc.; yuktasya — who is engaged; bhaktān — his disciples; ca — and; niyuñjataḥ — who engages; api — also; vande — I offer obeisances; guroḥ — of my spiritual master; śrī — auspicious; caraṇa-aravindam — unto the lotus feet

verses.translation: Śrī guru feels much contentment in satisfying Śrī Hari’s devotees with the four kinds of bhagavat-prasāda—that which is chewed, sucked, licked, and drunk. (By honoring such prasāda, material life is destroyed and true satisfaction, or the bliss of prema, is attained.) I adore the lotus feet of that śrī gurudeva.
verses.wbw: catuḥ — four; vidha — kinds; śrī — holy; bhagavat-prasāda — which have been offered to Kṛṣṇa; svādu — palatable; anna — (by) foods; tṛptān — spiritually satisfied; hari — (of) Kṛṣṇa; bhakta-saṅghān — the devotees; kṛtvā — having made; eva — thus; tṛptim — satisfaction; bhajataḥ — who feels; sadā — always; eva — certainly; vande — I offer obeisances; guroḥ — of my spiritual master; śrī — auspicious; caraṇa-aravindam — unto the lotus feet

verses.translation: At every moment, śrī gurudeva is experiencing intense greed in his heart to relish the unlimited sweetness of the holy names, forms, qualities, and pastimes of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava. I adore the lotus feet of that śrī gurudeva.
verses.wbw: śrī-rādhikā — (of) Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī; mādhavayoḥ — of Lord Mādhava (Kṛṣṇa); apāra — unlimited; mādhurya — conjugal; līlā — pastimes; guṇa — qualities; rūpa — forms; nāmnām — of the holy names; prati-kṣaṇa — at every moment; āsvādana — relishing; lolupasya — who aspires after; vande — I offer obeisances; guroḥ — of my spiritual master; śrī — auspicious; caraṇa-aravindam — unto the lotus feet

verses.translation: In carrying out the sakhīs’ arrangements for the perfection of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa’s amorous pastimes within the groves of Vṛndāvana, śrī guru is masterfully adept and thus especially dear to Them. I adore the lotus feet of that śrī gurudeva.
verses.wbw: nikuñja-yūnaḥ — of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; rati — (of) conjugal love; keli — (of) pastimes; siddhyai — for the perfection; yā yā — whatever; ālibhiḥ — by the gopīs; yuktiḥ — arrangements; apekṣaṇīyā — desirable; tatra — in that connection; ati-dākṣyāt — because of being very expert; ati-vallabhasya — who is very dear; vande — I offer obeisances; guroḥ — of my spiritual master; śrī — auspicious; caraṇa-aravindam — unto the lotus feet

verses.translation: Scriptures unanimously proclaim śrī guru to be sākṣāt-hari, directly Śrī Hari. This is a fact jointly corroborated by all saintly persons. Yet at the same time, śrī guru is very dear to Bhagavān. I adore the lotus feet of that śrī gurudeva (who is inconceivably one with and different from Bhagavān).
verses.wbw: sākṣāt — directly; hari-tvena — with the quality of Hari; samasta — all; śāstraiḥ — by scriptures; uktaḥ — acknowledged; tathā — thus; bhāvyate — is considered; eva — also; sadbhiḥ — by great saintly persons; kintu — however; prabhoḥ — to the Lord; yaḥ — who; priyaḥ — dear; eva — certainly; tasya — of him (the guru); vande — I offer obeisances; guroḥ — of my spiritual master; śrī — auspicious; caraṇa-aravindam — unto the lotus feet

verses.translation: Solely by the mercy of śrī guru one can receive the mercy of Bhagavān; without it, one cannot make any advancement. Meditate on and sing śrī guru’s glories at the three sacred junctions of the day. I adore the lotus feet of that śrī gurudeva.
verses.wbw: yasya — of whom (the spiritual master); prasādāt — by the grace; bhagavat — (of) Kṛṣṇa; prasādaḥ — the mercy; yasya — of whom; aprasādāt — without the grace; na — not; gatiḥ — means of advancement; kutaḥ api — from anywhere; dhyāyan — meditating upon; stuvan — praising; tasya — of him (the spiritual master); yaśaḥ — the glory; tri-sandhyam — three times a day (sunrise, noon, and sunset); vande — I offer obeisances; guroḥ — of my spiritual master; śrī — auspicious; caraṇa-aravindam — unto the lotus feet

verses.translation: That person who, during brāhma-muhūrta, loudly and attentively recites this Gurvāṣṭakam is sure to achieve direct service to the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the life and soul of Vṛndāvana, at the end of his current life (upon attaining vastu-siddhi, his eternal spiritual form).
verses.wbw: śrīmad-guror aṣṭakam — the eight verses glorifying the spiritual master; etad — this; uccaiḥ — very loudly; brāhme muhūrte — at the auspicious time of brāhma-muhūrta; paṭhati — recites; prayatnāt — with great care; yaḥ tena — by that person; vṛndāvana-nātha — the Lord of Vṛndāvana; sākṣāt — personally; sevā eva — service; labhyā — gain; januṣaḥ ante — at the end of life; eva — certainly

song-prabhupada-padma-stavakah.translation_source: Śrī Gauḍīya Gīti-guccha (GVP, 7th ed. 2016), «Śrī Prabhupāda-padma-stavakaḥ», pp. 260–263
translation_edits: v3: the stray verse number «(3)» after the translation removed
song-prabhupada-padma-stavakah.wbw_source: composed by Purohita Lipikāra (Mantrī A123) from the IAST and the GGG translation. kksongs.org/synonym/s/sujanarvudaradhitapada.html exists but was NOT used: it contradicts the GGG translation in many places (e.g. v1 «dhurandhara — one who bears a bow and arrow», v4 «siṁha — lion; varam — gold», v3 «arbuda — defeated», v5 «vipulī — exclusively», «bhuvaneṣu — to Lord of the world», «gaura-dayam — heart»)

verses.translation: His two lotus feet are worshiped by an unlimited number of saintly persons, and he is the most competent personality to lead the process of realization for this age, nāma-saṅkīrtana. His adorable lotus feet grant all kinds of benedictions and fearlessness. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura Prabhupāda.
verses.wbw: sujana — by saintly persons; arbuda — countless (lit. a hundred million); rādhita — worshiped; pāda-yugaṁ — whose two lotus feet; yuga-dharma — of the religion of the age (nāma-saṅkīrtana); dhurandhara — leading; pātra — personality; varam — the most competent; varada — all benedictions; abhaya — fearlessness; dāyaka — granting; pūjya — adorable; padaṁ — whose feet; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma; sadā — forever; prabhupāda-padam — unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda

verses.translation: He is the leader of the assembly of saints who are powerful in bhajana. He is most compassionate to the fallen, as he is their sole refuge. His inconceivable feet deceive the cheaters. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda.
verses.wbw: bhajana — in bhajana; ūrjita — powerful; sajjana — of saints; saṅgha — of the assembly; patiṁ — the leader; patita — to the fallen; adhika — most; kāruṇika — compassionate; eka — the sole; gatim — refuge; gati-vañcita — deprived of attainment; vañcaka — the cheaters; acintya — inconceivable; padaṁ — whose feet; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma; sadā — forever; prabhupāda-padam — unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda

verses.translation: His tall golden figure, which is very soft, mocks the pride of a golden lotus. His moonlike feet are worshiped by countless Cupids. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda.
verses.wbw: ati — very; komala — soft; kāñcana — golden; dīrgha — tall; tanuṁ — whose figure; tanu — by whose figure; nindita — mocked; hema — golden; mṛṇāla — of the lotus; madam — the pride; madana — Cupids; arbuda — countless; vandita — worshiped; candra — moonlike; padaṁ — whose feet; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma; sadā — forever; prabhupāda-padam — unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda

verses.translation: He is the pleasing moon for his servitor stars, and with the excellence of a roaring lion he removes inimical persons [causing them to flee in fear]. Choosing the shelter of his feet, the innocent attain auspiciousness. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda.
verses.wbw: nija — his own; sevaka — servitors; tāraka — for the stars; rañji — pleasing; vidhuṁ — the moon; vidhuta — removed; ahita — inimical persons; huṅkṛta — roaring; siṁha — lion; varam — excellent; varaṇa — choosing (the shelter); āgata — having come; bāliśa — the innocent; śanda — (which) grant auspiciousness; padaṁ — whose feet; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma; sadā — forever; prabhupāda-padam — unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda

verses.translation: He has widely spread the splendor of Śrī Gaurāṅga’s holy abode, Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma; he has specially glorified Śrī Gaurāṅga’s mercy throughout the whole world; and he has bestowed Gaurāṅga’s holy feet upon those who are most desperate for mercy. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda.
verses.wbw: vipulī-kṛta — widely spread; vaibhava — the splendor; gaura-bhuvaṁ — of Śrī Gaurāṅga’s holy abode (Śrī Navadvīpa-dhāma); bhuvaneṣu — throughout the world; vikīrtita — specially glorified; gaura-dayam — Śrī Gaurāṅga’s mercy; dayanīya-gaṇa — upon those most desperate for mercy; arpita — bestowed; gaura-padaṁ — Gaurāṅga’s holy feet; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma; sadā — forever; prabhupāda-padam — unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda

verses.translation: He is the eternal refuge and universal guru for the devotees of Śrī Gaurāṅga. He is always dedicated to the service of his holy master, Śrīla Gaura-kiśora dāsa Bābājī, and he is the abode of utmost honor for the feet of Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda.
verses.wbw: cira — eternal; gaura-jana — for the devotees of Śrī Gaurāṅga; āśraya — the refuge; viśva-guruṁ — the universal guru; guru — his holy master; gaura-kiśoraka — Śrīla Gaura-kiśora dāsa Bābājī; dāsya — to the service; param — dedicated; parama — utmost; ādṛta — honor; bhaktivinoda — for (the feet of) Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura; padaṁ — the abode; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma; sadā — forever; prabhupāda-padam — unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda

verses.translation: He shares renown with Raghunātha dāsa, Rūpa, and Sanātana Gosvāmīs and is glorified the world over for emulating the philosophical genius of Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī. He shares friendship with Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī and Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda.
verses.wbw: raghu — Śrī Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī; rūpa — Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī; sanātana — Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī; kīrti — the renown; dharaṁ — who shares; dharaṇī-tala — the world over; kīrtita — glorified; jīva-kavim — (for emulating) the philosophical genius Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī; kavirāja — Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī; narottama — Śrī Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura; sakhya — friendship; padaṁ — the abode; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma; sadā — forever; prabhupāda-padam — unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda

verses.translation: Out of mercy, he reveals himself as the embodiment of hari-kīrtana. He is an eternal associate of Lord Gaura, born to remove the great burden of the Earth. His nature is even more loving and affectionate than that of a father. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda.
verses.wbw: kṛpayā — out of mercy; hari-kīrtana — of hari-kīrtana; mūrti — the embodiment; dharaṁ — who reveals (lit. bears); dharaṇī — of the Earth; bhara — the burden; hāraka — removing; gaura-janam — the eternal associate of Lord Gaura; janaka — a father; adhika — more than; vatsala — loving; snigdha — affectionate; padaṁ — whose feet (nature); praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma; sadā — forever; prabhupāda-padam — unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda

verses.translation: He is a desire tree (of benedictions) for his surrendered servants. His patience and benevolence put a tree to shame. His divine feet are worshiped by the best of those who offer benedictions. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda.
verses.wbw: śaraṇāgata — surrendered; kiṅkara — for the servants; kalpa-taruṁ — a desire tree; taru — a tree; dhik-kṛta — put to shame; dhīra — in patience; vadānya — and benevolence; varam — the best; varada-indra-gaṇa — by the best of those who offer benedictions; arcita — worshiped; divya — divine; padaṁ — whose feet; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma; sadā — forever; prabhupāda-padam — unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda

verses.translation: He is the best amongst paramahaṁsas. He holds the treasure of the ultimate objective of life (kṛṣṇa-prema). He accepts the dress of a sannyāsī to uplift the fallen souls. His feet are carefully served by the best among sannyāsīs. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda.

verses.translation: He is a most beloved attendant of the daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu. I have taken shelter of his feet by keeping their dust [on my head]. Those feet possess immense and astonishing power to purify. I forever offer praṇāma unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda.
verses.wbw: vṛṣabhānu-sutā — of the daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu; dayita — most beloved; anucaraṁ — attendant; caraṇa — his feet; āśrita — having taken shelter of; reṇu — their dust; dharaḥ — keeping (on my head); tam — unto him; aham — I; mahat — immense; adbhuta — astonishing; pāvana — to purify; śakti — power; padaṁ — whose feet; praṇamāmi — I offer praṇāma; sadā — forever; prabhupāda-padam — unto the feet of Śrīla Prabhupāda

song-mangala-arati.translation_source: Śrī Gauḍīya Gīti-guccha (GVP, 7th ed. 2016), «Śrī Maṅgala Ārati» (Śrī Śrīmad Bhakti Prajñāna Keśava Gosvāmī Mahārāja), pp. 230–231

verses.translation: All glories to the auspicious forms of śrī guru and Śrī Gaura. All glories to the divine amorous love of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa.
verses.wbw: maṅgala — all glories, auspicious; śrī — śrī; guru-gaura — of guru and Gaura; maṅgala — auspicious; mūrati — to the forms; maṅgala — all glories; śrī — Śrī Śrī; rādhā-kṛṣṇa — of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; yugala — of the Divine Couple; pīriti — to the amorous love

verses.translation: All glories to Their niśānta-līlā, which awakens all-auspiciousness. All glories to Their ārati ceremony, which awakens within the hearts of the devotees.
verses.wbw: maṅgala — all glories; niśānta-līlā — to the niśānta-līlā (pastimes at the end of night); maṅgala — all-auspiciousness; udaye — awakens; maṅgala — all glories; ārati — to the ārati ceremony; jāge — awakens; bhakata-hṛdaye — within the hearts of the devotees

verses.translation: During Your slumber, the jīvas remain sleeping in this world, but upon Your rising, the whole world awakens.
verses.wbw: tomāra — Your; nidrāya — during slumber; jīva — the jīvas; nidrita — remain sleeping; dharāya — in this world; tava — Your; jāgaraṇe — upon rising; viśva — the whole world; jāgarita — awakened; haya — becomes

verses.translation: [O Lord!] Bestow Your beneficent glance upon the world, just now. May that most auspicious rati awaken in my heart.
verses.wbw: śubha — beneficent; dṛṣṭi — glance; karo — bestow; ebe — just now; (prabhu) — (O Lord); jagatera — the world; prati — upon; jāguka — may awaken; hṛdaye — in the heart; mora — my; sumaṅgalā — most auspicious; rati — rati

verses.translation: Many peacocks, male and female parrots, cuckoos, and other birds are present to herald Your auspicious awakening.
verses.wbw: mayūra — peacocks; śukādi — male parrots and others; sāri — female parrots; kato — many; pikarāja — cuckoos; maṅgala — auspicious; jāgara-hetu — to herald the awakening; koriche — are; virāja — present

verses.translation: The birds on the branches make the sweetest sounds. Their sweet chirping resounds auspiciously.
verses.wbw: sumadhura — the sweetest; dhvani — sounds; kare — make; jato — all; śākhī-gaṇa — the birds on the branches; maṅgala — auspiciously; śravaṇe — to the hearing; bāje — resounds; madhura — sweet; kūjana — chirping

verses.translation: In a pond filled with many varieties of flowers, lotuses sway to and fro. Gently billowing breezes carry their auspicious fragrance in all directions.
verses.wbw: kusumita — filled with flowers; sarovare — in a pond; kamala — lotuses; hillola — sway to and fro; maṅgala — auspicious; saurabha — fragrance; bahe — carry; pavana — breezes; kallola — gently billowing

verses.translation: Large cymbals, gongs, bells, conches, karatālas, and auspicious mṛdaṅgas resonate most sweetly.
verses.wbw: jhājhara — large cymbals; kāsara — gongs; ghaṇṭā — bells; śaṅkha — conches; karatāla — karatālas; maṅgala — auspicious; mṛdaṅga — mṛdaṅgas; bāje — resonate; parama — most; rasāla — sweetly

verses.translation: While the devotees perform maṅgala-ārati, this unfortunate Keśava (the servant of Śrī Keśava) sings nāma-saṅkīrtana.

song-vibhavari-sesa.wbw_source: kksongs.org/synonym/v/vibhavarisesa.html (BBT-style synonyms); headwords spelt as in our IAST (ḍ, v, ṁ, ’); v8 «mānasa-candra-cakora» composed by Purohita Lipikāra after the GGG translation, because the kksongs gloss («the moon of the gopīs’ minds…») contradicts it

verses.translation: Night is over, and the light [of dawn] is coming. Arise, O jīva, and give up your sleep! Chant the names of Hari, Mukunda, Murāri, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, and Hayagrīva!
verses.wbw: vibhāvarī — the night; śeṣa — has come to an end; āloka-praveśa — the light of dawn is entering; nidrā chāḍi’ — giving up your sleep; uṭho — arise; jīva — O soul; bolo’ hari hari — chant the holy names of Lord Hari; mukunda — the giver of liberation; murāri — the enemy of the Mura demon; rāma — the supreme enjoyer; kṛṣṇa — the all-attractive one; hayagrīva — the horse-headed incarnation

verses.translation: [Chant] Nṛsiṁha, Vāmana, Śrī Madhusūdana, Vrajendra-nandana, and Śyāma—the killer of Pūtanā and the destroyer of Kaiṭabha. All glories to the son of King Daśaratha, Lord Rāma!
verses.wbw: nṛsiṁha — the half-man, half-lion; vāmana — the dwarf brāhmaṇa; śrī madhusūdana — the killer of the Madhu demon; vrajendra-nandana — the beloved son of the King of Vraja; śyāma — who is blackish in complexion; pūtanā-ghātana — the slayer of the Pūtanā witch; kaiṭabha-śātana — the destroyer of the demon Kaiṭabha; jaya — all glories; dāśarathi-rāma — Lord Rāma, the son of King Daśaratha

verses.translation: He is the darling son of Yaśodā and the protector and maintainer of the cows, their pastures, the gopas, and the gopīs. He is the king of Vṛndāvana, the dearmost beloved of the gopīs, and the consort of Śrīmatī Rādhikā. In the entire world, His beauty is unsurpassed.
verses.wbw: yaśodā-dulāla — the darling of mother Yaśodā; govinda — the giver of pleasure to the cows; gopāla — the protector of the cows; vṛndāvana-purandara — the monarch of the Vṛndāvana forest; gopī-priya-jana — the beloved of the gopīs; rādhikā-ramaṇa — the lover of Rādhikā; bhuvana-sundara-vara — the most beautiful personality in all the worlds

verses.translation: He is the killer of Rāvaṇa, the butter thief, the stealer of the young gopīs’ garments, the protector of the cows of Vraja, the guardian of the gopas, and the flute player who enchants the minds of all.
verses.wbw: rāvaṇāntakara — who brought about the end of the demon Rāvaṇa; mākhana-taskara — who stole the older gopīs’ butter; gopī-jana-vastra-hārī — who stole the younger gopīs’ clothes; vrajera rākhāla — a cowherd boy of Vraja; gopa-vṛnda-pāla — the protector of the cowherd boys; citta-hārī — who steals the hearts of all; vaṁśī-dhārī — who always holds a flute

verses.translation: He is the object of great yogīs’ worship, the beautiful son of Nanda, and the remover of fear from the residents of Vraja. His form, which is like a fresh rain cloud, enchants the mind, and He captivates all with His artistry in flute-playing.
verses.wbw: yogīndra-vandana — worshiped by the best of yogīs; śrī nanda-nandana — the delightful son of Nanda; vraja-jana-bhaya-hārī — who removes all the fears of the inhabitants of Vraja; navīna nīrada — who is the color of a fresh rain cloud; rūpa manohara — whose form is enchanting; mohana-vaṁśī-bihārī — who looks very charming wandering about playing His flute

verses.translation: He is the darling son of Yaśodā, the heroic killer of Kaṁsa, the performer of nectarean pastimes in the pleasure-groves of Vraja, the enjoyer of the rāsa dance in the arena of the kadamba forest, and the resident of Vṛndāvana Forest.
verses.wbw: yaśodā-nandana — the delightful son of Yaśodā; kaṁsa-nisūdana — the killer of King Kaṁsa; nikuñja-rāsa-vilāsī — who sports the rāsa dance amongst the garden groves; kadamba-kānana rāsa-parāyaṇa — who is fond of engaging in the rāsa dance underneath the kadamba trees; vṛndā-vipina-nivāsī — who resides in the forest of Vṛndā-devī

verses.translation: He is the enhancer of bliss and the abode of prema. He is the transcendental Cupid who aims His flower arrows [at the gopīs, by which He increases transcendental desires in them]. He gives pleasure to the hearts of the gopīs, and He is the abode of all good qualities.
verses.wbw: ānanda-vardhana — who increases the ecstasy of His devotees; prema-niketana — the reservoir of all love; phula-śara — flowered arrows; yojaka — who uses; kāma — the transcendental Cupid; gopāṅganā-gaṇa-citta-vinodana — the pleasure of the cowherd girls’ hearts; samasta-guṇa-gaṇa-dhāma — the abode of all wonderful qualities

verses.translation: He is the life and soul of Yamunā, He is absorbed in amorous pastimes, and He is the cakora bird who subsists on the rays emanating from the moon of Śrī Rādhā’s mind. O mind, always heed my words and sing Kṛṣṇa’s glories in the form of these holy names, which are full of nectar.
verses.wbw: yāmuna-jīvana — the life of the River Yamunā; keli-parāyaṇa — who is always absorbed in amorous pastimes; mānasa-candra-cakora — the cakora bird who subsists on the rays of the moon of Śrī Rādhā’s mind; nāma-sudhā-rasa — the nectarean mellows of these holy names; gāo — please sing; kṛṣṇa-yaśa — the glories of Śrī Kṛṣṇa; rākho vacana — please obey this advice; mana mora — O my dear mind

song-vraja-dhama-mahimamrta.translation_source: Śrī Gauḍīya Gīti-guccha (GVP, 7th ed. 2016), «Jaya Rādhe, Jaya Kṛṣṇa» (Kṛṣṇadāsa), pp. 150–151
song-vraja-dhama-mahimamrta.wbw_source: kksongs.org/synonym/j/jayaradhejayakrsna1.html (BBT-style synonyms); headwords spelt as in our IAST (jāṅhā, jāṅhārā, jato, jāhā, vrajete, koilo, kahe); edits: v4 «mother and father, Nanda and Yaśodā» → «father and mother, Nanda and Yaśodā» (word order of the verse), v6 «cowherd boyfriend of Kṛṣṇa» → «friend of Kṛṣṇa» (Madhumaṅgala is a brāhmaṇa, not a cowherd), v8 «of whom» → «who»; v11 «dīna — fallen; kṛṣṇadāsa — Kṛṣṇadāsa» composed after the GGG translation (kksongs «Dīna Duḥkhi Kṛṣṇadāsa» does not fit it)

verses.translation: All glories to Śrī Rādhā, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, and the divine forest of Śrī Vṛndāvana. All glories to Śrī Govinda, Gopīnātha, and Madana-mohana [the three presiding deities of Vṛndāvana].
verses.wbw: jaya rādhe jaya kṛṣṇa — all glories to Śrī Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa; jaya vṛndāvana — glories to the transcendental realm of Vṛndāvana; śrī govinda gopīnātha madana-mohana — glories to the three presiding Deities of Vṛndāvana: Govinda, Gopīnātha and Madana-mohana

verses.translation: All glories to Śyāma-kuṇḍa, Rādhā-kuṇḍa, and Govardhana Hill. All glories to the river Yamunā (Kālindī) and to the great forest known as Gokula Mahāvana [where Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma performed Their childhood pastimes].
verses.wbw: śyāma-kuṇḍa — glories to the personal lake of Śyāma; rādhā-kuṇḍa — glories to the personal lake of Rādhā; giri-govardhana — glories to Govardhana Hill; kālindī yamunā jaya — glories to the Yamunā river, known as Kālindī, the daughter of the Kalinda mountain; jaya mahāvana — glories to the great forest of Mahāvana, the place of Kṛṣṇa’s childhood pastimes

verses.translation: All glories to Keśī-ghāṭa [where Kṛṣṇa killed the Keśī demon], Vaṁśīvaṭa [the banyan tree that Kṛṣṇa stood under and attracted the gopīs by playing His flute], and to the twelve forests of Vraja, where the son of Nanda performed His pastimes.
verses.wbw: keśī-ghāṭa — glories to Keśī-ghāṭa, where Kṛṣṇa killed the horse demon; vaṁśī-vaṭa — glories to the Vaṁśī-vaṭa tree, where Kṛṣṇa sits and calls the gopīs with His flute; dvādaśa-kānana — glories to the twelve forests of Vraja; jāṅhā — where; saba — all; līlā — pastimes; koilo — performed; śrī nanda-nandana — the son of Nanda Mahārāja

verses.translation: All glories to Śrī Nanda and Śrī Yaśodā [Kṛṣṇa’s father and mother]. All glories to the cowherd boys, headed by Śrīdāma [the older brother of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and Anaṅga Mañjarī]. All glories to the cows and calves of Vraja.
verses.wbw: śrī nanda-yaśodā jaya — glories to Kṛṣṇa’s divine father and mother, Nanda and Yaśodā; jaya gopa-gaṇa — glories to the assembly of cowherd boys; śrīdāmādi jaya — glories to the cowherd boy leaders headed by Śrīdāmā; jaya dhenu-vatsa-gaṇa — glories to the herds of cows and calves

verses.translation: All glories to Śrī Vṛṣabhānu and the beautiful Kīrtidā [Rādhārāṇī’s father and mother]. All glories, all glories to Paurṇamāsī [the guru of the cowherd community; the mother of Sāndīpani Muni; the grandmother of Madhumaṅgala and Nāndī-mukhī; and the disciple of Devarṣi Nārada]. All glories to the damsels of Vraja.
verses.wbw: jaya vṛṣabhānu — glories to Rādhā’s father; jaya kīrtidā-sundarī — glories to Rādhā’s beautiful mother; jaya paurṇamāsī — glories to the elderly Paurṇamāsī, the personality of Yogamāyā; jaya ābhīra-nāgarī — glories to the cowherd women of Vraja

verses.translation: All glories, all glories to Gopīśvara Śiva, who resides within Vṛndāvana [to protect the holy dhāma]. All glories, all glories to Kṛṣṇa’s young brāhmaṇa friend, Madhumaṅgala.
verses.wbw: jaya jaya gopīśvara — glories to the presence of Lord Śiva as Gopīśvara Mahādeva; vṛndāvana-mājha — in the midst of Vṛndāvana; jaya jaya kṛṣṇa-sakhā — glories, all glories to the friend of Kṛṣṇa; baṭu — Śrī Madhumaṅgala; dvija-rāja — the monarch of the twice-born brāhmaṇas

verses.translation: All glories to Rāma-ghāṭa [where Balarāma performed His rāsa dance]. All glories to Balarāma, the son of Rohiṇī. All glories, all glories to all the residents of Vṛndāvana.
verses.wbw: jaya rāma-ghāṭa — glories to the landing on the Yamunā river where Balarāma sported the rāsa dance; jaya rohiṇī-nandana — glories to the son of Rohiṇī (Balarāma); jaya jaya vṛndāvana-vāsī — glories, all glories to the inhabitants of Vṛndāvana; jato — all; jana — the people

verses.translation: All glories to the wives of the proud Vedic brāhmaṇas and to the wives of the serpent Kālīya, all of whom attained the lotus feet of Govinda through pure bhakti.
verses.wbw: jaya dvija-patnī — glories to the wives of the Vedic brāhmaṇas; jaya nāga-kanyā-gaṇa — glories to the wives of the Kāliya serpent; bhaktite — in devotion; jāṅhārā — who; pāilo — had attained; govinda-caraṇa — the lotus feet of Govinda

verses.translation: All glories to the circular arena of the rāsa dance. All glories to Rādhā and Śyāma. All glories, all glories to the most beautiful rāsa-līlā.
verses.wbw: śrī rāsa-maṇḍala jaya — glories to the circular arena of the rāsa dance; jaya rādhā-śyāma — glories to Rādhā-Śyāma; jaya jaya rāsa-līlā — glories, all glories to the rāsa-līlā; sarva-manorama — which captures the minds of all

verses.translation: All glories, all glories to ujjvala-rasa (śṛṅgāra-rasa), which is the essence and most excellent of all rasas and which is known as the parakīya-bhāva of Vraja.
verses.wbw: jaya jaya ujjvala-rasa — glories, all glories to the ujjvala-rasa, the conjugal mellow; sarva-rasa-sāra — the quintessence of all ecstatic mellows; parakīyā-bhāve — in the mood of paramourship; jāhā — which; vrajete pracāra — is manifest only in the realm of Vraja

verses.translation: Remembering the lotus feet of Śrī Jāhnavā-devī [Nityānanda Prabhu’s consort], this fallen Kṛṣṇadāsa performs nāma-saṅkīrtana.
verses.wbw: śrī jāhnavā-pāda-padma — the lotus feet of Lord Nityānanda’s śakti, Śrī Jāhnavā-devī; koriyā smaraṇa — remembering; dīna — fallen; kṛṣṇadāsa — Kṛṣṇadāsa; kahe nāma-saṅkīrtana — sings the names of the Lord

song-gaura-arati.translation_source: Śrī Gauḍīya Gīti-guccha (GVP, 7th ed. 2016), «Śrī Gaura Ārati», pp. 238–239
song-gaura-arati.wbw_source: kksongs.org/synonym/j/jayajayagoracander.html (BBT-style synonyms); headwords spelt as in our IAST (gorācāṅdera, dakṣiṇe, nitāicāṅda, bāme, karena, kare); «Srī/Siva/Sukadeva/Thākura» → «Śrī/Śiva/Śukadeva/Ṭhākura»; v3 «performing» → «perform»

verses.translation: All glories, all glories to the beautiful ārati ceremony of Śrī Gaura-candra, performed in a forest on the banks of the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā) River. It attracts the minds of everyone in the universe.
verses.wbw: jaya jaya — all glories, all glories; gorācāṅdera — of the moonlike Lord Caitanya; āratiko śobhā — the beautiful ārati ceremony; jāhnavī-taṭa-vane — in a grove on the banks of the Ganges river; jaga-mana-lobhā — attracting the minds of all living entities in the universe

verses.translation: On the right [of Gaurāṅga] is the moonlike Nityānanda Prabhu, and on the left is Gadādhara Paṇḍita. Nearby are Advaita Ācārya and Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita, who holds an umbrella [over the Lord’s head].
verses.wbw: dakṣiṇe nitāicāṅda — on His right side is the moonlike Lord Nityānanda; bāme gadādhara — on His left is Śrī Gadādhara; nikaṭe advaita — nearby stands Śrī Advaita; śrīnivāsa chatra-dhara — and Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura is holding an umbrella

verses.translation: Śrī Gaura-candra is seated on a jeweled throne, and Lord Brahmā and the other demigods perform His ārati.
verses.wbw: bosiyāche — is sitting; gorācāṅda — Lord Gaura-candra; ratna-siṁhāsane — upon a jeweled throne; ārati karena — perform the ārati ceremony; brahmā-ādi deva-gaṇe — the demigods, headed by Lord Brahmā

verses.translation: Narahari Sarakāra and others fan the Lord with cāmaras, while Sañjaya Paṇḍita, Mukunda Daṭṭa, Vāsudeva Ghoṣa, and others sing [His glories].
verses.wbw: narahari-ādi — Narahari Sarakāra and other associates; kori’ cāmara ḍhulāya — fanning Him with cāmara whisks; sañjaya-mukunda vāsu-ghoṣa-ādi — the devotees headed by Sañjaya, Mukunda and Vāsu Ghoṣa; gāya — are singing

verses.translation: The resonating conch, the ringing bell, the chiming karatālas, and the sweet rhythm of the mṛdaṅga converge together to create the topmost rasa.
verses.wbw: śaṅkha bāje — conchshells resound; ghaṇṭā bāje — bells resound; bāje karatāla — hand cymbals resound; madhura mṛdaṅga bāje — sweet clay drums resound; parama rasāla — supremely sweet and relishable to hear

verses.translation: Śrī Gaura’s brilliant face conquers [the glow of] many millions of moons, and the garland of forest flowers about His neck glimmers splendidly.
verses.wbw: bahu-koṭi — many millions; candra — of moons; jini’ — conquering; vadana ujjvala — the brilliance of Lord Caitanya’s face; gala-deśe — around His neck; vana-mālā — the garland of forest flowers; kare jhalamala — shines

verses.translation: Lord Śiva, Śukadeva Gosvāmī, and Nārada Muni become choked with prema. Thus, Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura beholds the glories of Śrī Gaurāṅga.
verses.wbw: śiva-śuka-nārada — Lord Śiva, Śukadeva Gosvāmī, and Nārada Muni; preme — with the ecstasy of transcendental love; gada-gada — their voices are choked; bhakativinoda — thus Ṭhākura Bhaktivinoda; dekhe — beholds; gorāra sampada — the glory of Lord Caitanya

song-yugala-arati.translation_source: Śrī Gauḍīya Gīti-guccha (GVP, 7th ed. 2016), «Śrī Yugala Ārati», pp. 239–240
song-yugala-arati.wbw_source: composed by Purohita Lipikāra (Mantrī A123) from the IAST and the GGG translation, word division as in the Russian пословный перевод (kksongs.org has the song, jayajayaradhakrsna.html, but no word-for-word; not in GGG 2016 or Versebase)

verses.translation: All glories, all glories to the meeting of the Divine Couple, Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. The sakhīs, led by Lalitā-devī, perform Their ārati ceremony.
verses.wbw: jaya — all glories; jaya — all glories; rādhā-kṛṣṇa — of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa; yugala-milana — to the meeting of the Divine Couple; ārati — the ārati ceremony; karoye — perform; lalitādi — led by Lalitā-devī; sakhī-gaṇa — the sakhīs

verses.translation: The beautiful threefold bending form of Kṛṣṇa, the enchanter of Cupid, wears yellow silk garments and a crown of peacock feathers, captivating the minds of all.
verses.wbw: madana-mohana-rūpa — the form of Kṛṣṇa, the enchanter of Cupid; tri-bhaṅga-sundara — beautiful, bending in three places; pītāmbara — yellow silk garments; śikhi-puccha-cūḍā — a crown of peacock feathers; manohara — captivating the mind

verses.translation: To the left of the charming Mādhava is the beautiful daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu, Śrīmatī Rādhikā. She wears blue garments, Her complexion is the color of molten gold, and She is well endowed with beauty and other fine qualities.
verses.wbw: lalita-mādhava-bāme — to the left of the charming Mādhava; vṛṣabhānu-kanyā — the daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu; nīla-vasanā — wearing blue garments; gaurī — of golden complexion; rūpe — with beauty; guṇe — with qualities; dhanyā — well endowed

verses.translation: She is adorned with various ornaments that sparkle and shimmer. Her radiant face enchants the mind of Śrī Hari.
verses.wbw: nānā-vidha — various; alaṅkāra — ornaments; kare — make; jhalamala — sparkle and shimmer; hari-mana-vimohana — enchanting the mind of Śrī Hari; vadana — face; ujjvala — radiant

verses.translation: The sakhīs, led by Viśākhā-devī, sing in various melodies, while other priya-narma-sakhīs fan the Divine Couple with cāmaras.
verses.wbw: viśākhādi — led by Viśākhā-devī; sakhī-gaṇa — the sakhīs; nānā — various; rāge — in melodies; gāya — sing; priya-narma-sakhī — the priya-narma-sakhīs; jato — other; cāmara-ḍhulāya — fan with cāmaras

verses.translation: Hoping to attain the lotus feet of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava, Bhaktivinoda happily floats in happiness at the lotus feet of the sakhīs.
verses.wbw: śrī — Śrī Śrī; rādhā-mādhava-pada-sarasija-āśe — hoping to attain the lotus feet of Rādhā-Mādhava; bhakativinoda — Bhaktivinoda; sakhī-pade — at the lotus feet of the sakhīs; sukhe — in happiness; bhāse — floats
